description: Framework Directive for prudential regulation of insurance and reinsurance undertakings in the EU. Three-pillar structure: Pillar 1 (quantitative capital requirements), Pillar 2 (governance and ORSA), Pillar 3 (reporting and disclosure). Insurance undertakings are obliged entities under AMLR for life insurance and investment-linked products.

Omnibus directive amending Solvency II: proportionality for small and non-complex undertakings, sustainability risk, long-term guarantee measures, and supervisory convergence improvements. ESG and climate risk integrated into ORSA.

The risk-based capital requirement under Solvency II. Represents the amount of funds required to ensure the insurance undertaking can meet its obligations with 99.5% probability over a one-year horizon. Can be calculated using standard formula or internal model.

The minimum level of capital below which policyholders would be exposed to an unacceptable risk level. MCR triggers supervisory ladder of intervention: fall below MCR → supervisory authority withdraws authorisation. Calibrated between 25%-45% of SCR.

Internal process by which an insurance undertaking assesses its own risk profile and solvency needs, both now and prospectively under stress scenarios. Must consider all material risks including emerging risks such as climate change. Required at least annually. AML/TF risk must be considered in ORSA.

Annual public disclosure document required under Solvency II Pillar 3. Covers: business and performance, system of governance, risk profile, valuation, and capital management. Published on insurance undertaking's website.

canonical_name: Life Insurance as Obliged Entity (AMLR Scope)
description: Life insurance undertakings and intermediaries dealing with life insurance and investment-linked products are obliged entities under AMLR Art. 3. Subject to CDD when: establishing relationship, paying out policies ≥€10,000, assigning policies, or if ML/TF suspicion exists. Beneficiary of policy must be identified at payout.

Insurer must identify and verify the beneficiary of a life insurance policy as part of CDD. Must screen beneficiary against PEP lists and sanctions lists. If beneficiary is a PEP, enhanced due diligence applies. Timing: before policy proceeds are paid out.

Insurance products where the policyholder's return is linked to the performance of investment funds. Higher AML risk than pure protection products due to investment component. AMLR covers as obliged entity scope. PRIIPs KID disclosure required.

Reinsurance undertakings face ML/TF risk through: fictitious reinsurance arrangements, premium manipulation, collusion in claim payments. Not always classified as obliged entities for standard CDD but subject to AML controls as part of group policies.

Undertaking-specific model for calculating SCR, subject to EIOPA/national supervisor approval. Requires pre-application process, use test, statistical quality, calibration, profit/loss attribution, model validation, and documentation standards.

canonical_name: Solvency II Art. 41-49 — System of Governance
description: Solvency II governance requirements: adequate transparent system of governance, four key functions (risk management, compliance, internal audit, actuarial), fit & proper requirements for key persons, remuneration policy. Interacts with AML compliance function requirements.

Mandatory governance functions under Solvency II Art. 44-48: (1) Risk management function; (2) Compliance function; (3) Internal audit function; (4) Actuarial function. AML compliance officer role sits within or alongside the compliance function.

Life insurance undertakings operate under both Solvency II (prudential) and AMLR (AML/CFT). Solvency II governance framework provides infrastructure for AML compliance function. ORSA must consider ML/TF risk. CDD under AMLR supplements Solvency II Know Your Customer requirements.

Insurance undertakings subject to CSRD sustainability disclosure must also integrate ESG risks into their ORSA. Climate transition risk and physical risk increasingly material. CSRD and Solvency II Review align ESG risk integration requirements.

Insurance undertakings process health data (sensitive personal data) as part of their core business. GDPR Art. 9 conditions for processing health data apply. AML data retention (AMLR Art. 77) must be balanced against GDPR data minimisation and purpose limitation.

canonical_name: EIOPA — European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority
description: EU supervisory authority for insurance and occupational pensions. Issues binding technical standards and guidelines on Solvency II. Promotes supervisory convergence among national insurance supervisors. Issues opinions on specific topics including AML in insurance.

canonical_name: PRIIPs Regulation — Packaged Retail Insurance-Based Investment Products
description: Regulation (EU) 1286/2014 requiring a standardised Key Information Document (KID) for packaged retail investment and insurance-based products. Covers unit-linked and with-profits insurance products. KID must disclose costs, risks, and scenarios.

CDD process for life insurance obliged entities: (1) Identify and verify policyholder at contract conclusion; (2) Identify beneficiary; (3) Verify beneficiary at payout or assignment; (4) Screen against PEP lists and sanctions lists; (5) EDD for PEP beneficiaries; (6) SAR if ML/TF suspicion.

Known insurance ML typologies: (1) Premium overpayment and refund request; (2) Early policy surrender (accepting penalty to clean funds); (3) Policy assignment to third party; (4) Fictitious claims; (5) Life settlement transactions with multiple resale.
